newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Selectivity advised as Korea relaxes foreign rules.
newsitem.headline: Selectivity advised as Korea relaxes foreign rules.

text.p: Investors in the South Korean stock market should be selective when reshuffling their portfolios to reflect Friday's increase in foreign ownership limits, SBC Warburg said in a research report.
South Korea on Friday relaxed restrictions on foreign ownership of its companies to 23 percent from 20 percent. Another relaxation is expected later this year.

"We recommend that investors use 2 May, 1997, as an opportunity to reshuffle their portfolios, reducing exposure to companies that face the prospect of a sharp drop in earnings over the next 12 months," said SBC Warburg executive director Richard Samuelson.

In their place, SBC Warburg recommended in a recent report that Samsung Electronics, Hankook Tyre, POSCO, Cheil Jedang, Korea Chemical, LG Information & Communication, SK Telecom, Housing & Commercial Bank, Shinhan Bank, Samsung Fire and Marine Insurance
SBC Warburg said selectivity would be required to counter continuing high volatility over the coming year, with an index target band of between 625 and 800 throughout 1997.
Although some macroeconomic improvements boded well for the market in the second half of this year, SBC Warburg remained neutral on the market over the next six months.

Earnings per share should grow 20 percent this year and more than that next year, driven by an expected increase in banking sector earnings and a strong rebound in the earnings of the electronics and oil refining sectors and Korean Air.
The performance of the electronics sector would be assisted by a fall in dynamic random access memory prices and an appreciating won, SBC Warburg said.

"Investors may wonder why we are not more bullish on the market with such strong EPS forecasts, however our neutral view reflects the expected low return on equity for the manufacturing sector in 1998," Samuelson said.
Weak economic fundamentals and political uncertainty in the run-up to December's presidential elections would keep the market volatile throughout the year.

Any further corporate bankruptcies would push the index to the lower end of SBC Warburg's target band, with strong EPS growth and historically weak valuations expected to spur the index to 800 by the end of the year.
